# Implementation Plan: crews Listener Delivery Observability Logging
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-listener-observability-logging"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-listener-observability-logging/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Add three additive, behavior-preserving observability log lines to the **crews** plugin
(`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews`) so an operator can diagnose listener-delivery timing
gaps from `crews.log` alone, without manual cross-referencing of mailbox `sentAt` timestamps
against listener arm/timeout wall-clocks.

Root incident: a self-imposed `--timeout-ms` (20 min) expired ~2 s **before** an impl `done`
report landed (mailbox-history seq 417 `sentAt 02:03:45` vs listener timeout `02:03:43`). The
member report then sat in an un-armed mailbox until the next arm's `via=initial` scan. Diagnosing
this required hand-correlating three separate facts (the message `sentAt`, the listener timeout
wall-clock, and the gap during which no listener was armed). The three log lines below make each
of those facts visible inline at the moment they matter.

This is **observability-only**: no change to listener delivery, drain, timeout, heartbeat,
mailbox append/consume, or version behavior. The listener stdout JSON envelope shape is
**unchanged** (the new fields go only into `crews.log` lifecycle lines, never the stdout
envelope). Two small pure helper functions are extracted so the age computation and the
queued-while-unarmed predicate are unit-testable.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews` is a CommonJS, JavaScript-only plugin (no package-level
`package.json`; "Typecheck passes" = `node --check <file>` per the crews `AGENTS.md`). Full
suite runs via `node tests/run.js` (one fresh Worker per test file; targets <60 s on Windows).
Tests use the local `tests/lib/assert` harness; `tests/consume-mailbox-epoch-fence.test.js` is
the canonical pattern for asserting `crews.log` lines from a deterministic unit test.

Key edit points (verified against the primary checkout — the plan worktree intentionally has the
submodule uninitialized, so impl reads/edits happen in an `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule
worktree, see Risk Areas):

- **`lib/listener-loop.js`** — the `crews.js arm` listener process.
  - `runListenerLoop(argv, io, opts)` (~line 139) destructures `timeoutMs` (~line 147) and sets
    `const start = Date.now()` (~line 164). `timeoutMs` may be `null` (indefinite listener — the
    default since v1.2.7).
  - `deliver(reason)` (~line 331) drains via `consumeMailbox(...)`, and on a non-empty batch
    logs (line ~347):
    `listener delivered name=${name} crew=${crew} via=${reason} count=${messages.length}`
  - `bail(reason)` (~line 359) logs the timeout (line ~362):
    `listener timeout name=${name} crew=${crew} reason=${reason} waitedMs=${Date.now() - start}`
  - `deliver`/`bail` are closures inside `runListenerLoop`, so `start` and `timeoutMs` are in
    scope at both log sites — no manifest re-read needed.
  - Module exports (lines ~403-409): `USAGE, parseListenerArgs, runListenerLoop,
    isStdoutNonInteractive, formatNoNewListenerAdvisory`.

- **`hooks/mailbox.js`** — mailbox append/consume primitives + `appendLog(line, cwd)` (~line 926;
  re-exported from `hooks/config.js`, writes timestamped lines to `<cwd>/.crews/logs/crews.log`,
  rotates at 64 KB, and **swallows logging errors** — so all three new log lines are best-effort
  by construction and can never throw into the delivery/append paths).
  - `appendMailboxWithSender(name, crew, cwd, message, sender, opts)` (~line 403) is the **single
    chokepoint** through which `appendMailbox` (~line 449), `appendSystemMailbox` (~line 489),
    AND `appendOperatorMailbox` (~line 542) all route. It already reads the recipient manifest
    (`const manifest = readManifest(safeName, safeCrew, cwd) || {}`, ~line 411) inside the
    mailbox lock, **before** `writeJsonAtomic(mailboxPath, mailbox)` (~line 439). The envelope's
    `kind` is on `envelope.kind`; `sentAt` is stamped as an ISO string at line ~433.

- **`hooks/actor-state.js`** — `deriveListenerState(manifest)` (~line 60). Returns the raw
  `manifest.listenerState` when set, but **demotes** a stale `armed` manifest (dead PID via
  `isProcessAlive`, or heartbeat older than `HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS_LOCAL = 5 min`) to `exited`. The
  `isProcessAlive` call (an OS process check) fires only on the `listenerState === 'armed'` +
  fresh-heartbeat branch.

- **`hooks/protocol/manifest.js`** — there is **no `armedAt` manifest field**. The closest are
  `lastListenerSpawnAt` and `lastHeartbeatAt`, but `lastListenerSpawnAt` is refreshed by every
  heartbeat tick (so it is NOT a stable "when this listener armed" anchor). The correct
  `armedAt` for the listener's own lifetime is the loop-local `start` timestamp.

- **Envelopes** carry a top-level `sentAt` ISO string (set in `appendMailboxWithSender`,
  line ~433); the drained `messages[]` returned by `consumeMailbox` therefore each carry `sentAt`.

### Technical Constraints

- Logging is observability-only. Do **not** alter the listener stdout envelope (`{type:"messages",
  ...}` / `{type:"timeout", ...}`), the drain semantics, the heartbeat/epoch ownership, the
  mailbox lock discipline, or any review-required stamping. Existing tests must pass unmodified
  (the change is purely additive to `crews.log` text + two new exported pure helpers).
- crews has no transpile/typecheck step; the verification gate is `node --check` on each touched
  `.js` file plus the full `node tests/run.js` suite.
- The mailbox append path holds the mailbox lock; the new log write must reuse the already-read
  `manifest` (no second manifest read, no extra lock).
- Version literal lives in 6 stamped files + 1 assertion; only `scripts/bump-version.js` is the
  sanctioned writer (see Files to Modify). crews lives in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule, so
  the ship is a two-commit (submodule-first, then codexu pointer) flow.

## Approach

### Architecture

Three log-line enrichments at four existing `appendLog` / write sites, plus two extracted pure
helpers for testability. No new modules, no new manifest fields, no stdout-envelope change.

**Change 1 + Change 3 — listener-loop.js lifecycle lines.** In `runListenerLoop`, compute two
loop-local quantities at each log site:
- `armedAtAgeMs = Date.now() - start` (how long this listener had been armed at the moment of
  delivery/timeout). `start` is the listener's true arm time; do NOT read manifest
  `lastListenerSpawnAt` (heartbeat-refreshed, per copilot+self research).
- `timeoutMs` is already in scope (may be `null` → render the literal `null`).

  - `deliver(reason)` delivered line becomes:
    `listener delivered name=<n> crew=<c> via=<reason> count=<N> timeoutMs=<ms|null> armedAtAgeMs=<ms>`
    and, **only when `reason === 'initial'`**, additionally ` oldestMsgAgeMs=<ms>` where
    `oldestMsgAgeMs = computeOldestMsgAgeMs(messages, Date.now())` (Change 1). A large
    `oldestMsgAgeMs` on `via=initial` is the tell-tale that the message sat in an un-armed mailbox.
  - `bail(reason)` timeout line becomes:
    `listener timeout name=<n> crew=<c> reason=<reason> waitedMs=<ms> timeoutMs=<ms|null> armedAtAgeMs=<ms>`

**Change 1 helper — `computeOldestMsgAgeMs(messages, now)`** (new pure exported fn in
`lib/listener-loop.js`): parse each `message.sentAt` with `Date.parse`, drop `NaN`, return
`now - min(parsed)`; return `null` when `messages` is empty/missing or no entry has a parseable
`sentAt`. The delivered line includes `oldestMsgAgeMs=<n>` only when the value is non-null AND
`reason === 'initial'`.

**Change 2 — mailbox.js queued-while-unarmed line.** At the `appendMailboxWithSender` chokepoint,
**after** the successful `writeJsonAtomic(mailboxPath, mailbox)` (~line 439, still inside the
lock), evaluate the already-read `manifest` with a new pure predicate
`isQueuedWhileUnarmed(manifest)` and, when true, emit
`mail-queued-no-listener name=<recipient> crew=<crew> kind=<kind>` via `appendLog`. `kind` =
`envelope.kind || opts.kind || sender.routingKind || 'message'`. Because the predicate sits at the
shared chokepoint it covers `appendMailbox`, `appendSystemMailbox`, and `appendOperatorMailbox` in
one place (the seed names appendMailbox/appendSystemMailbox; the chokepoint is the
strictly-superset-correct site and avoids duplicated code / a second manifest read).

> **Best-effort guard (plan-review High).** `appendLog` (mailbox.js:926-938) runs
> `getLogPath(cwd)` + `ensureDir(path.dirname(file))` *outside* its internal try/catch, so it CAN
> throw (e.g. a logs-dir creation failure). Since this new call lands *after* the mailbox write
> succeeded, an unguarded throw would convert an observability write into a caller-visible send
> failure — violating "no behavior change". The new call site MUST be wrapped in its own
> `try { appendLog(...); } catch (_) { /* observability is best-effort */ }`. (The existing
> listener-loop delivered/timeout `appendLog` calls are pre-existing throw sites and are NOT new
> exposure — change 1/3 only appends fields to those existing call strings.)

**Change 2 predicate — `isQueuedWhileUnarmed(manifest)`** (new exported helper in
`hooks/mailbox.js`). **Recommendation (revised after 3-way review consensus): use the *derived*
state.** Return `deriveListenerState(manifest) !== 'armed'` (lazy `require('./actor-state')` at the
call to respect the existing mailbox.js↔actor-state.js require cycle, which the codebase already
handles via lazy requires). The raw `manifest.listenerState !== 'armed'` form (which the seed's
literal wording suggests) is **rejected** because it is wrong in both directions for a log named
`mail-queued-no-listener`: (a) it misses a stale `armed` manifest whose listener is provably dead
(crashed without `markExited`, or heartbeat older than 5 min) — `deriveListenerState` demotes that
to `exited`; and (b) it false-positives on legacy timestamp-only manifests (no `listenerState`
field but `lastListenerSpawnAt` set with no exit), where `deriveListenerState` correctly infers
`armed`. The derived form costs at most one `isProcessAlive` (`process.kill(pid,0)`) syscall, and
only on the explicit-`armed`-with-live-PID branch (not a spawn). The root-incident case (listener
`exited` via timeout 2 s before the report) is covered by both forms. The predicate is deterministic
for a given (manifest, clock, liveness) — not strictly pure, since `deriveListenerState` reads the
clock and (on the live-armed branch) `process.kill(pid,0)` — and is unit-testable: synthetic manifests drive every branch, and the stale-armed branch is exercised via
heartbeat-staleness (no reliance on real PID liveness).

### Implementation Strategy

All `node` commands below assume cwd `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews` unless stated otherwise
(crews is a JS-only plugin under that submodule path; impl edits happen in a submodule worktree —
see Risk Areas).

1. **US-001 (listener-loop.js):** add `computeOldestMsgAgeMs` (exported pure fn); enrich the
   `deliver` delivered line (timeoutMs + armedAtAgeMs always; oldestMsgAgeMs only on
   `via=initial`); enrich the `bail` timeout line (timeoutMs + armedAtAgeMs). Verify with
   `node --check lib/listener-loop.js`.
2. **US-002 (mailbox.js):** add `isQueuedWhileUnarmed` (exported helper, derived-state form); emit
   `mail-queued-no-listener` at the post-write point inside `appendMailboxWithSender`, wrapped in
   its own try/catch (best-effort guard). Verify with `node --check hooks/mailbox.js`.
3. **US-003 (tests):** new `tests/listener-delivery-observability.test.js` covering BOTH layers —
   (a) pure-helper unit tests: `computeOldestMsgAgeMs` (oldest-wins, null on empty/unparseable,
   ignores NaN entries) and `isQueuedWhileUnarmed` (armed→false; never-armed/exited/recoverable→
   true; stale-armed-via-heartbeat→true; legacy-timestamp-only→false; null manifest→true); (b)
   end-to-end listener-loop tests (subprocess or injected-IO, mirroring `tests/listener.test.js` /
   `tests/dispatcher-arm-listener.test.js`): an `initial` delivery asserts `crews.log` contains the
   new `listener delivered ... timeoutMs=... armedAtAgeMs=... oldestMsgAgeMs=...` fields and an
   explicit timeout asserts `listener timeout ... timeoutMs=... armedAtAgeMs=...`, while the stdout
   envelope key-set is unchanged; (c) queued-while-unarmed e2e (mirroring
   `consume-mailbox-epoch-fence.test.js`) that `mail-queued-no-listener` is logged for an unarmed
   recipient and NOT for an armed one, exercising `appendMailbox`, `appendSystemMailbox`, AND
   `appendOperatorMailbox` (or a source-level assertion that the log line exists only inside
   `appendMailboxWithSender`, proving no per-entry-point duplication); (d) a failure-seam assertion
   that an `appendLog`/logging failure cannot fail the append (the try/catch guard). Run full suite:
   `node tests/run.js`.
4. **US-004 (submodule version + docs — member-owned):** from cwd `ai-developer-toolkit`,
   `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js 3.11.0` → 6 stamps; verify
   `node plugins/crews/tests/version.test.js`; prepend `plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md` `## 3.11.0`
   entry; add a `## v3.11.0` section to `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md` documenting the three log lines +
   the two helpers + the observability-only non-goals; AND correct the existing crews `AGENTS.md`
   "Version layout" section (currently stale: says 5 files and omits
   `plugins/crews/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`) to the current 6-stamp reality. Re-run the full suite
   `node plugins/crews/tests/run.js` as the final gate after all edits. These all live **inside** the
   `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule and are committed on the impl member's submodule topic branch.

5. **Ship steps (lead-owned, AFTER the submodule branch merges to the submodule's main) — NOT impl
   member commits:** in codexu, update the `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table (crews
   3.10.0→3.11.0) and record the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule pointer (gitlink) bump in a
   separate codexu commit. Per the repo's two-commit rule the parent commit can only record a SHA;
   it must not bundle uncommitted submodule edits.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Three additive `crews.log` lifecycle log-line enrichments (Changes 1-3).
- Two extracted pure exported helpers (`computeOldestMsgAgeMs`, `isQueuedWhileUnarmed`).
- One new unit+e2e test file.
- crews version bump 3.10.0→3.11.0 (6 stamps + version test) + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md section.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to listener delivery/drain/timeout/heartbeat/epoch semantics.
- Any change to the listener stdout JSON envelope shape.
- Any new manifest field (no persisted `armedAt`; use loop-local `start`).
- Adding the new fields to the inbox-history `via` row or any non-`crews.log` surface.
- Cross-engine (claude/copilot/codex) hook-shim changes — none are needed (the log sites are
  engine-agnostic).
- Surfacing the new diagnostics in `list-members`, `review-mail`, or any UI.

## Risk Areas

- **Submodule two-commit flow.** crews lives in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule. Impl MUST
  create its worktree INSIDE that submodule (`ai-developer-toolkit/.worktrees/<task-id>` on
  `ralph/<task-id>`), commit + push the submodule branch first, then record the codexu submodule
  pointer bump in a second codexu commit. Do NOT mix uncommitted submodule edits into a codexu
  commit. (Plan worktree has the submodule uninitialized — fine; the plan only writes markdown
  under `.ralph/jobs`.)
- **Append-path predicate IO + require cycle.** `isQueuedWhileUnarmed` now uses
  `deriveListenerState(manifest)` (3-way review consensus), which adds at most one
  `isProcessAlive` (`process.kill(pid,0)`) syscall and only on the explicit-`armed`-with-live-PID
  branch — cheap, not a spawn, and `appendMailbox` is not a tight loop. `mailbox.js` must reach
  `deriveListenerState` via a **lazy** `require('./actor-state')` (actor-state.js already requires
  mailbox.js at top level — the codebase resolves this exact cycle with lazy requires elsewhere).
- **New `appendLog` call is a throw site after the mailbox write.** `appendLog` runs
  `getLogPath`/`ensureDir` outside its internal try/catch, so the change-2 call MUST be wrapped in
  its own `try/catch` — otherwise a logs-dir failure would fail the send *after* the mailbox was
  written, breaking the no-behavior-change guarantee. (Covered by the failure-seam AC.)
- **`timeoutMs` is `null` by default.** Render it as the literal `null` (do not coerce to `0` or
  omit) so the indefinite-listener case is unambiguous in the log.
- **`armedAtAgeMs` ≈ `waitedMs` on the timeout line.** On `bail`, `armedAtAgeMs = Date.now() -
  start` is numerically close to the existing `waitedMs`. This is intentional and harmless (the
  field is added for symmetry with the delivered line, which has no other timing); call it out in
  the AGENTS.md note so a future reader doesn't "dedupe" it.
- **`sentAt` parse robustness.** `computeOldestMsgAgeMs` must tolerate missing/malformed `sentAt`
  (drop `NaN`, return `null` if none parse) so a single bad envelope never throws inside the
  listener delivery path.
- **Version stamp drift.** Always bump via `scripts/bump-version.js` (3 plugin manifests + 3
  marketplace indexes); hand-editing reliably misses one (historically the Copilot manifest).
  `tests/version.test.js` is the guard. Do NOT add the new helpers to `hooks/config.js` (snapshotted
  by `tests/split-export-compat.test.js`) — keep them leaf-module exports.

## Acceptance Criteria

All commands run from cwd `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews` unless a different cwd is named.

- [ ] `node --check lib/listener-loop.js` and `node --check hooks/mailbox.js` both pass.
- [ ] `lib/listener-loop.js` exports a pure `computeOldestMsgAgeMs(messages, now)` returning
  `now - min(parseable sentAt)`, or `null` when none parse / empty input; a unit test asserts
  oldest-wins, NaN-skip, and the null cases.
- [ ] `hooks/mailbox.js` exports a small `isQueuedWhileUnarmed(manifest)` helper defined as
  `deriveListenerState(manifest) !== 'armed'`, returning `false` for a live/legitimate `armed`
  manifest (incl. legacy timestamp-only manifests that derive to `armed`) and `true` for
  never-armed / exited / recoverable / stale-armed (dead-PID or stale-heartbeat) / null manifest;
  a unit test asserts each of those branches (stale-armed exercised via heartbeat-staleness so the
  test stays deterministic without depending on real PID liveness). Note: the helper is not
  strictly pure — `deriveListenerState` reads the clock and (on the live-armed branch)
  `process.kill(pid,0)` — but is deterministic for a given (manifest, clock, liveness) input.
- [ ] The delivered log line includes `timeoutMs=<ms|null>` and `armedAtAgeMs=<ms>` on every
  delivery, and additionally `oldestMsgAgeMs=<ms>` exactly when `via=initial` (and the value is
  non-null). A deterministic listener-loop test (subprocess or injected-IO) asserts these fields
  appear in `crews.log` for an `initial` delivery.
- [ ] The timeout log line includes `timeoutMs=<ms|null>` and `armedAtAgeMs=<ms>`. A deterministic
  test drives an explicit timeout and asserts these fields appear in the `crews.log` timeout line.
- [ ] An end-to-end test asserts `mail-queued-no-listener name=<recipient> crew=<crew> kind=<kind>`
  is appended to `crews.log` when the recipient is not (derived-) `armed`, and is NOT appended when
  it is `armed`. The test exercises the `appendMailbox`, `appendSystemMailbox`, AND
  `appendOperatorMailbox` entry points (or includes a source-level assertion that the log line
  exists only inside `appendMailboxWithSender`, proving no per-entry-point duplication).
- [ ] The new append-path `appendLog(...)` call is enclosed in a local `try/catch` inside
  `appendMailboxWithSender`. Because that call uses the module-local `appendLog` binding,
  monkey-patching the exported `appendLog` would NOT exercise it — so verification is a **source
  assertion** that the new call site is try/catch-guarded (a runtime failure-injection test would
  require introducing an injectable logging seam, which is out of scope).
- [ ] The listener stdout envelopes are unchanged in shape: the `{type:"messages",...}` key set
  (`type`, `count`, `name`, `crew`, `sessionId?`, `via`) and the `{type:"timeout",...}` key set
  (`type`, `reason`, `name`, `crew`, `sessionId?`, `waitedMs`) gain **no new keys** and lose none,
  and no message body is added to the `{type:"messages"}` envelope. The test tolerates `sessionId`
  being present or absent (omitted by `JSON.stringify` when undefined in the no-session-env path)
  rather than doing a brittle exact-key comparison. No existing test is modified to accommodate a
  behavior change (additive edits only).
- [ ] Full suite `node tests/run.js` (run from `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews`) passes
  (existing + new file) on Windows under the documented ceiling. This is re-run as the FINAL gate
  **after** the version bump + CHANGELOG/AGENTS edits (not only `node tests/version.test.js`).
- [ ] crews version is `3.11.0` across all 6 stamped files (3 plugin manifests + 3 marketplace
  indexes); `node tests/version.test.js` passes; `plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md` carries a `## 3.11.0`
  entry and `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md` a `## v3.11.0` section. Version is bumped via
  `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js 3.11.0` (from cwd `ai-developer-toolkit`), never by
  hand. The crews `AGENTS.md` existing "Version layout" section (currently stale — says 5 files and
  omits `plugins/crews/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`) is corrected to the current **6**-stamp reality
  in the same edit. The codexu `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table + submodule pointer bump are
  lead-owned ship steps (separate codexu commit), not impl-member commits.

## Suggested Decomposition

The whole feature is one small, cohesive crews-plugin change (~2 source files + 1 test file + the
shared version/CHANGELOG/AGENTS surface). US-001 and US-002 touch disjoint source files
(`listener-loop.js` vs `mailbox.js`) but US-003 imports both new helpers and US-004 stamps the
shared version/CHANGELOG/AGENTS files, so the natural shape is a **single serial cluster** for one
implementer pass. There is no parallelism benefit at this size, and the version/CHANGELOG/AGENTS
writes are a known conflict surface that must not be split across parallel members.

### Cluster: listener-observability
- Stories: [US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004]
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md`, `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md`, the 6
  version-stamp files]; exclusive per story=[`lib/listener-loop.js` (US-001),
  `hooks/mailbox.js` (US-002), `tests/listener-delivery-observability.test.js` (US-003)];
  risk=low.
- `execution_mode` rationale: Single implementer, serial. The stories share the version/CHANGELOG/
  AGENTS surface and the test depends on both new helpers, so splitting across parallel members
  would create version-file and import conflicts for no throughput gain on a ~2-file change.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-listener-observability-logging/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition .ralph/jobs/crews-listener-observability-logging/suggested-decomposition.json`

## Open Questions

- **Q1 (predicate: raw vs derived listenerState) — RESOLVED to derived.** 3-way plan-review
  consensus (Claude + Codex + self) flipped this from the seed's literal raw
  `manifest.listenerState !== 'armed'` to `deriveListenerState(manifest) !== 'armed'`. Rationale:
  the raw form is wrong in both directions for a `mail-queued-no-listener` diagnostic — it misses
  a stale `armed` manifest whose listener is provably dead, and false-positives on legacy
  timestamp-only manifests that derive to `armed`. The derived form costs at most one cheap
  `isProcessAlive` syscall on the live-armed branch. This is a deliberate, documented deviation
  from the seed's literal wording in favor of correctness. [RESOLVED via review consensus]
- **Q2 (oldestMsgAgeMs scope).** The seed says compute/log `oldestMsgAgeMs` "when via===initial".
  The plan logs it ONLY on `via=initial` deliveries (its diagnostic meaning — "sat in an un-armed
  mailbox" — is specific to the up-front sweep). `via=poll`/`via=watch` deliveries are near-real-
  time so the age would be ~0 and add noise. [INFERRED — matches seed wording.]
- **Q3 (version target + helper export scope) — RESOLVED.** crews `3.10.0 → 3.11.0` (minor). The
  rationale rests on the **new observable log-line contract** (a brand-new `mail-queued-no-listener`
  line + new structured fields operators/tooling may grep), NOT on new public API — the two helpers
  are exported from their **leaf modules only** for unit testing and are deliberately NOT added to
  the `hooks/config.js` compatibility surface (which is snapshotted by
  `tests/split-export-compat.test.js`). The independent Codex research pass suggested `3.10.1`
  (patch); crews history is mixed (e.g. v3.6.3 shipped a display-only feature as a third-digit
  bump). `3.11.0` is the recommended target; `3.10.1` remains an acceptable operator override if
  the new log lines are judged pure-patch. Confirm the impl member does NOT bump until ship, and
  bumps only via `scripts/bump-version.js`. [RESOLVED — review-driven; operator may override to
  3.10.1]

lead spawns an impl-phase member that runs:

`/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-listener-observability-logging/plan.md --autonomous`

where `<job_dir>` is `.ralph/jobs/crews-listener-observability-logging` once the plan branch is
merged. The impl member targets the **`ai-developer-toolkit` submodule** (worktree inside that

codexu `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table + submodule pointer bump are lead-owned ship
steps). Drive impl through Phase 5a (code review-fix) and Phase 5b (docs review-fix) to terminal
before merge.

After merging, clean up the plan worktree with
`/plan-with-ralph cleanup crews-listener-observability-logging`.
